context.title: Jabez and the Clans
context.summary: More of Judah's clans are listed, broken by the brief story of Jabez's prayer. The chapter then turns to Simeon's families, towns, and expansion.
context.background: Simeon's land lay inside Judah's territory (Joshua 19:1, 9), and over time the tribe was largely absorbed into Judah. Notes about craftsmen — linen workers and royal potters (vv. 21–23) — show that these lists record trades and towns as well as names.

customs.note: The name sounds like the Hebrew word for pain or sorrow. His prayer asks that his life not match his name.

watchFor: Jabez's prayer is the only extended story in a long list of names (vv. 9–10).
The Simeonites' expansion is dated to the days of Hezekiah (v. 41).

people.name: Pharez
people.summary: Pharez,, breach, the son of Judah (Neh. 11:4). “The chief of all the captains of the host for the first month” in the reign of David was taken from his family (1 Chr. 27:3).

people.name: Hezron
people.summary: The older of the two sons of Pharez (Gen. 46:12).

people.name: Hur
people.summary: The husband of Miriam, Moses’ sister (Ex. 17:10-12). He was associated with Aaron in charge of the people when Moses was absent on Sinai (Ex. 24:14).

people.name: Caleb
people.summary: One of the three sons of Hezron of the tribe of Judah. He is also called Chelubai (1 Chr. 2:9).

people.name: Shobal
people.summary: One of the sons of Caleb, and a descendant of Hur (1 Chr. 2:50, 52; 4:1, 2).

people.name: Ephratah
people.summary: The second wife of Caleb, the son of Hezron, mother of Hur, and grandmother of Caleb, who was one of those that were sent to spy the land (1 Chr. 2:19, 50).

people.name: Helah
people.summary: Rust, (1 Chr. 4:5, 7), one of the wives of Ashur.

people.name: Naarah
people.summary: A girl, the second of Ashur’s two wives, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:5, 6).

people.name: Hepher
people.summary: The second son of Asher (1 Chr. 4:6).

people.name: Temeni
people.summary: One of the sons of Ashur, the father of Tekoa (1 Chr. 4:6).

people.name: Coz
people.summary: A descendant of Judah. 1 Chr. 4:8, “Coz;” R.V., “Hakkoz.”

people.name: Harum
people.summary: Elevated, (1 Chr. 4:8), a descendant of Judah.

people.name: Jabez
people.summary: A descendant of Judah, of whom it is recorded that “God granted him that which he requested” (1 Chr. 4:9, 10).

people.name: Othniel
people.summary: Lion of God, the first of the judges. His wife Achsah was the daughter of Caleb (Josh. 15:16, 17; Judg. 1:13). He gained her hand as a reward for his bravery in leading a successful expedition against Debir.

people.name: Kenaz
people.summary: Caleb’s younger brother, and father of Othniel (Josh. 15:17), whose family was of importance in Israel down to the time of David (1 Chr. 27:15).

people.name: Caleb
people.summary: The son of Jephunneh (Num. 13:6; 32:12; Josh. 14:6, 14). He was one of those whom Moses sent to search the land in the second year after the Exodus.

people.name: Jephunneh
people.summary: The father of Caleb, who was Joshua’s companion in exploring Canaan (Num. 13:6), a Kenezite (Josh. 14:14).

people.name: Elah
people.summary: The second of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

people.name: Naam
people.summary: Pleasantness, one of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

people.name: Mered
people.summary: Rebellion, one of the sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

people.name: Jalon
people.summary: Lodger, the last of the four sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

people.name: Miriam
people.summary: 1 Chr. 4:17, one of the descendants of Judah.

people.name: Shammai
people.summary: The son of Rekem and father of Maon, A Judahite.

people.name: Jered
people.summary: A son of Ezra probably (1 Chr. 4:18).

people.name: Amnon
people.summary: One of the sons of Shammai, of the children of Ezra (1 Chr. 4:20; comp. 17).

people.name: Zoheth
people.summary: Snatching (?), one of the sons of Ishi (1 Chr. 4:20).

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

people.name: Jokim
people.summary: Whom Jehovah has set up, one of the descendants of Shelah (1 Chr. 4:22).

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26).

people.name: Jachin
people.summary: The fourth son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10), called also Jarib (1 Chr. 4:24).

people.name: Jemuel
people.summary: One of Simeon’s five sons (1 Chr. 4:24), called also Jemuel (Gen. 46:10).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: One of the sons of Simeon (Gen. 46:10; Ex. 6:15).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Amaziah
people.summary: The father of Joshah, one of the Simeonite chiefs in the time of Hezekiah (1 Chr. 4:34).

people.name: Jehu
people.summary: A Simeonite prince during the reign of Hezekiah.

people.name: Adiel
people.summary: A family head of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

people.name: Jaakobah
people.summary: Heel-catcher, a form of the name Jacob, one of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

people.name: Allon
people.summary: The son of Jedaiah, of the family of the Simeonites, who expelled the Hamites from the valley of Gedor (1 Chr. 4:37).

people.name: Hezekiah
people.summary: Son of Ahaz (2 Kings 18:1; 2 Chr. 29:1), whom he succeeded on the throne of the kingdom of Judah. He reigned twenty-nine years (B.C. 726-697).

places.name: Cozeba
places.summary: (1 Chr. 4:22), the same as Chezib and Achzib, a place in the lowlands of Judah (Gen. 38:5; Josh. 15:44).

places.name: Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Gederah
places.summary: The fortress; a fortified place, a town in the plain (shephelah) of Judah (Josh. 15:36). This is a very common Canaanite and Phoenician name.

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Well of the oath, or well of seven, a well dug by Abraham, and so named because he and Abimelech here entered into a compact (Gen. 21:31). On re-opening it, Isaac gave it the same name (Gen. 26:31-33).

places.name: Hazar-shual
places.summary: Village or enclosure of the jackal, a city on the south border of Judah (Josh. 15:28; Neh. 11:27).

places.name: Moladah
places.summary: Birth, a city in the south of Judah which fell to Simeon (Josh. 15:21-26; 19:2).

places.name: Bilhah
places.summary: Faltering; bashful, Rachel’s handmaid, whom she gave to Jacob (Gen. 29:29). She was the mother of Dan and Naphtali (Gen. 30:3-8). Reuben was cursed by his father for committing adultry with her (35:22; 49:4).

places.name: Tolad
places.summary: Productive, a town of Simeon, in the south of Judah (1 Chr. 4:29).

places.name: Bethuel
places.summary: A southern city of Judah (1 Chr. 4:30); called also Bethul (Josh. 19:4) and Bethel (12:16; 1 Sam. 30:27).

places.name: Hormah
places.summary: Banning; i.e., placing under a “ban,” or devoting to utter destruction. After the manifestation of God’s anger against the Israelites, on account of their rebellion and their murmurings when the spies returned to the camp at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Paran, with an evil report of the land, they quickly repented of their conduct, and presumed to go up “to the head of the mountain,” seeking to enter the Promised Land, but without the presence of the Lord, without the ark of…

places.name: Ziklag
places.summary: A town in the Negeb, or south country of Judah (Josh. 15:31), in the possession of the Philistines when David fled to Gath from Ziph with all his followers.

places.name: Etam
places.summary: A village of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:32). Into some cleft (“top,” A.V.,; R.V., “cleft”) of a rock here Samson retired after his slaughter of the Philistines (Judg. 15:8, 11).

places.name: Rimmon
places.summary: One of the “uttermost cities” of Judah, afterwards given to Simeon (Josh. 15:21, 32; 19:7; 1 Chr. 4:32). In Josh. 15:32 Ain and Rimmon are mentioned separately, but in 19:7 and 1 Chr. 4:32 (comp. Neh. 11:29) the two words are probably to be combined, as forming together the name of one place, Ain-Rimmon=the spring of the pomegranate.

places.name: Tochen
places.summary: Measured, a town of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:32).

places.name: Baal
places.summary: The name of a place inhabited by the Simeonites, the same probably as Baal-ath-beer (1 Chr. 4:33; Josh. 19:8).

places.name: Gedor
places.summary: 1 Chr. 4:39, the Gederah of Josh. 15:36, or the well-known Gerar, as the LXX. read, where the patriarchs of old had sojourned and fed their flocks (Gen. 20:1, 14, 15; 26:1, 6, 14).
